# UI Skills Root

You are the routing layer for UI Skills.

This skill is shown by `npx ui-skills start` and is also available in the registry.

Use it when an agent in Codex, Cursor, or Claude Code has a clear UI goal.

If the goal is unclear, ask one short question.

If the goal is clear, choose the right category, load the smallest useful skill context, then implement.

## Protocol

1. decide if the task is UI-related
2. if not, return `no skill needed`
3. identify the likely category
4. inspect that category with the CLI
5. select the smallest useful skill set
6. load only selected skill(s)
7. implement using that context

## CLI

```bash
npx ui-skills start
npx ui-skills categories
npx ui-skills list --category <category>
npx ui-skills get <slug>
```

## Selection Rules

Prefer 1 skill.

Use 2 only when the task needs two clear angles.

Use 3 only for broad review, redesign, or multi-surface work.

Never use more than 3.

Route by topic, then stack, then specificity.

Prefer specific skills over broad skills.

Prefer framework-specific skills when the stack is obvious.

For quick cleanup, prefer the most specific craft, visual, or layout skill available.

If unsure, inspect categories and pick the safest narrow skill.

- when the user corrects the harness routing with wording like `did you use "ccx"` and then clarifies Codex should stay on Codex -> do not silently reroute requested model/harness combinations mid-run [Task 1][Task 2]
- when the user asks for a four-way comparison -> preserve the full requested matrix and keep failed requested routes as evidence instead of collapsing or substituting them [Task 2]
- when the user says a transcript or evidence drawer `never load` and sends screenshots -> treat it as a real browser-visible bug and verify the endpoint/UI directly, not just by reading code [Task 4]
- when the user asks to `use nuqs` and persist compare/filter state in the URL -> make the query string the durable source of truth and verify reload/back/clear behavior in the browser [Task 5]
- when the user interrupts a benchmark run with `stop everything now !!` -> stop immediately, preserve the raw evidence, and resume existing sessions instead of creating duplicate fresh runs [Task 6]
- when the user says `update all the prompt and all the logics to always ask : use pnpm` and wants one sub-agent per project -> treat pnpm-only policy plus delegated per-project migration as the default for repo-wide benchmark maintenance [Task 7]
- when the user asks to `verify all app run "pnpm build"` and be ready to test `without ruinninig it` -> prefer build-only readiness checks and avoid starting servers unless explicitly needed [Task 7]
- when the user provides a multi-entry benchmark matrix with repeated model names on different harness/effort pairs -> preserve every requested row and do not collapse same-model entries into one run [Task 9]

## Reusable knowledge

- `run-benchmark` can be extended locally when the catalog lacks a canonical prompt slug; this run added `elysian-taste-challenge` and mapped it to `https://code.melvynx.dev/prompts/elysian-taste-challenge/v1` instead of inventing prompt text [Task 1]
- the quick validator is optional in this environment because the local Python stack lacked `PyYAML` (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'`) [Task 1]
- the final verified run directories were `runs/20260712T185814Z-claude-fable-5-cc`, `runs/20260712T190813Z-gpt-5-6-luna-codex`, `runs/20260712T190813Z-gpt-5-6-sol-codex`, plus the intentionally preserved failed route `runs/20260712T185814Z-gpt-5-6-sol-cc` [Task 2][Task 3]
- benchmark outputs are not proven by transcript completion alone; verify the generated app/output independently with `npm run build` for Vite apps or `node --check script.js` plus HTML-document checks for standalone outputs, then normalize missing metadata such as `run.json` [Task 3]
- historical benchmark evidence should be resolved by run identity/date/model/harness/task, not only by visible app path, and very large transcript JSONL files should be condensed for UI display while preserving the original file on disk [Task 4]
- `benchmark-compare` was running on `127.0.0.1:9080` during the transcript-loading fix, and direct endpoint checks were the decisive proof when in-app browser actions hit policy limits [Task 4]
- for `benchmark-compare`, `NuqsAdapter` belongs at the TanStack Router root, compare selection should use push history, filter typing should use replace history, and defaults can be removed from the URL automatically [Task 5]
- resumed benchmark sessions should append new evidence files such as `transcript-resume-1.jsonl` and `final-resume-1.txt`; validators must scan every `transcript*.jsonl` and `final*.txt` file present instead of assuming a single transcript [Task 6]
- GPT models on the Claude Code family route through `ccx`, not `cc`; the blocked sixth `elysian-taste-challenge/v2` run failed before model invocation because the same-day app output path already existed, not because the prompt or validator was wrong [Task 6]
- the benchmark repo's centralized policy surfaces are `.agents/skills/run-benchmark/scripts/run-benchmark.sh`, `verify-benchmark-run.sh`, `validate-benchmark-run.sh`, `.agents/rules/benchmark-runs.md`, and `AGENTS.md`; this is where pnpm-only instructions and build-policy checks should be enforced [Task 7]
- installed-project policy audits in this repo should ignore `runs/**`, `.next/**`, `.output/**`, and `node_modules/**` when searching for actionable npm usage [Task 7]
- the final pnpm/build-readiness sweep proved `27` installed app roots, `27` policy passes, and `27` ready build artifacts; the only genuine blocker was missing `@types/react` / `@types/react-dom` in `timezone-checker/2026-04-24-gpt-5-5` [Task 7]
- `benchmark-compare/package.json` defines both `dev` and `start` as `vite dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9080`, so launch guidance for the compare app should be `cd benchmark-compare && pnpm start`, then open `http://127.0.0.1:9080` [Task 8]
- canonical prompt resolution in this repo is local and versioned under `content/prompts/<slug>/`; use the numerically highest local `v<number>.md` instead of fetching the website when a benchmark references a known prompt slug [Task 9]
- for GPT models on the Claude Code harness family, `ccx` accepts `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-luna`; repeated identical model/harness/task pairs are recorded with suffixes like `-2` and `-3` [Task 9]
- `validate-benchmark-run.sh` requires `screenshot.png` and `render.json` in addition to transcript and metadata files, so browser proof artifacts must be generated before calling a run fully validated [Task 9]

## Failures and how to do differently

- do not change harnesses midstream unless the user explicitly asks; a mistaken `ccx` correction had to be undone here [Task 2]
- if the benchmark runner races during concurrent post-processing (`app_name: unbound variable`, `--arg: command not found`), trust preserved per-run artifacts and re-run verification rather than treating the runner crash as total failure [Task 2][Task 3]
- if a requested route fails with `model_not_found`, preserve that failure and keep the requested matrix intact instead of substituting another model or harness [Task 2]
- use absolute paths or the correct `cwd` for verification commands; a wrong-directory check caused a spurious `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` during the first validation pass [Task 3]
- if evidence loading looks empty, check the historical lookup/indexing path and transcript payload size before blaming the frontend renderer; both were real contributors here [Task 4]
- once URL-backed state is wired with `nuqs`, do not double-parse the same query via TanStack `validateSearch`; that produced `values.map is not a function` during the first attempt [Task 5]
- if a resumed run is blocked by an existing app output path, preserve the blocker as evidence instead of overwriting or renaming the historical output directory [Task 6]
- repo-wide npm-to-pnpm scans must exclude dependency trees and generated folders; the first broad scan produced false positives inside `node_modules` [Task 7]
- when answering a simple launch question in this repo, narrow immediately to the target subproject; the first search surface contains many benchmark packages, so root-level commands are easy to overgeneralize [Task 8]
- if a `ccx` retry says `No conversation found with session ID`, preserve that failed evidence and start a fresh identical rerun instead of substituting another model or hiding the failure [Task 9]
- if one validated app still shows the wrong model title or console 404s, treat that as an output-quality defect even when `validation_failures=0`; screenshot existence alone is not enough [Task 9]
- if `run-benchmark.sh` throws a post-run shell syntax error near line 400 after producing artifacts, verify shell syntax before relying on the script for further reruns in this environment [Task 9]
